candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the entire text of an XML Schema document (or of any file whose root element is in the http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema namespace and whose URI ends in .xsd), for example a third-party schema the victim opens or a schema referenced from a project. The attacker can embed a DOCTYPE with parameter/general entity declarations whose SYSTEM identifiers point to local files (file:///etc/passwd) or to internal/remote URLs, and reference them in element/attribute content or xs:documentation/annotation content. The victim's security setting resolveExternalEntities=false is ignored for this path.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: Checked that the default XML path is hardened: LSPXMLParserConfiguration follows resolveExternalEntities (default false), sets disallow-doctype-decl per settings and installs a Xerces SecurityManager with entityExpansionLimit (64000) and maxOccur (5000). Checked that DOMUtils.newSAXParserFactory used by AssociateGrammarCommand sets disallow-doctype-decl=true. Checked that XSDValidator receives validationSettings but only calls isRelatedInformation(); nothing in the XSD preparser disables DOCTYPE, external entities, or sets a SecurityManager. No test sources exist in this snapshot to confirm runtime behavior; feature support of XMLSchemaLoader/XMLGrammarPreparser for these Xerces features is inferred from the code and Xerces semantics, not executed.
candidates.impact: Out-of-band/local file read and SSRF from the language-server process on behalf of an attacker-supplied schema; expanded entity data can be reflected into diagnostics and documentation shown/returned to the client; lack of an entity-expansion limit on this preparser permits entity-expansion denial of service. The user's explicit external-entity security setting is silently bypassed.
candidates.prerequisites: LemMinX diagnostics enabled (the default) and the victim opens/edits a crafted XSD or XML-Schema-rooted file; textDocument/didOpen triggers validation after ~500 ms without further user action. Network reachability of internal endpoints or existence/readability of local files applies for SSRF/file-read variants.
candidates.root_cause: XSDValidator.doDiagnostics() unconditionally sets Xerces features http://apache.org/xml/features/external-general-entities and http://apache.org/xml/features/external-parameter-entities to true on the LSPXMLGrammarPreparser used to parse/validate an opened XML Schema document. The XMLValidationSettings passed into the method (resolveExternalEntities, default false; disallowDocTypeDecl) are used only for related-information handling and are never consulted here, unlike the regular XML path in LSPXMLParserConfiguration where both features follow the settings. No disallow-doctype-decl and no Xerces SecurityManager/entity-expansion limit is applied on this preparser either.
candidates.title: External XML entities forced ON during XSD validation, ignoring resolveExternalEntities/disallowDocTypeDecl settings (XXE)
candidates.trace: XMLTextDocumentService.didOpen -> triggerValidationFor(...) -> XMLLanguageService.publishDiagnostics -> XMLDiagnostics.doDiagnostics -> XSDDiagnosticsParticipant.doDiagnostics (DOMUtils.isXSD(document) true) -> XSDValidator.doDiagnostics -> new LSPXMLGrammarPreparser() with XMLSchemaLoader -> setFeature(EXTERNAL_GENERAL_ENTITIES, true) and setFeature(EXTERNAL_PARAMETER_ENTITIES, true) -> preparseGrammar(XML_SCHEMA, inputSource built from the document text) with the LSPXMLEntityResolver wrapper -> DefaultURIResolverExtension / XMLCacheResolverExtension resolve entity SYSTEM ids -> local file content or remote resource is read and entity-expanded; Xerces messages/arguments derived from expanded content flow into LSP Diagnostics (LSPErrorReporterForXSD) / hover content, and remote SYSTEM ids cause server-side requests.
candidates.unverified: Runtime confirmation that Xerces XMLSchemaLoader expands the crafted external entity into an LSP-visible diagnostic/hover (depends on Xerces message arguments); exact payload behavior and how much file content is reflected. Also not verified whether upstream LemMinX at this revision intended these features to be true for legitimate entity-based schemas.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-611: Improper Restriction of XML External Entity Reference (XXE); CWE-918/CWE-400 as secondary effects

coverage_summary: Scope: 444 files under the assigned source root (org.eclipse.lemminx/src/main plus docs, build and CI files; no src/test directory exists in the snapshot). I read or searched the diagnostics/validation stack (XMLValidator, XSDValidator, LSPXMLParserConfiguration, LSPXMLEntityManager, LSPXMLEntityResolver, LSPSAXParser, ExternalXMLDTDValidator, XMLModelHandler/AwareParserConfiguration), URI resolution and caching (CacheResourcesManager, XMLCacheResolverExtension, XMLCatalogResolverExtension, XSD/XSL URI resolvers, URIResolverExtensionManager, FilesUtils), server entry points (XMLServerLauncher, XMLServerSocketLauncher, XMLWorkspaceService, XMLTextDocumentService), extension commands, settings/defaults, and the DOM parser; performed targeted sweeps for ProcessBuilder/exec, ScriptEngine, reflection, URL/file open, SAX/DOM/XSD parser factories, and setFeature calls. Prioritized untrusted-XML-content -> parser/resource-resolution paths.
limitations: No runtime execution or exploit validation was performed (read-only review); the XXE behavior is inferred from source and Xerces semantics.
No upstream diff/patch, CVE/advisory data, or ground-truth data was consulted (prohibited), so I cannot state whether these XSD entity features are a regression or longstanding upstream code.
Large service/utility classes (XMLCompletions, XMLPositionUtility, XMLFormatter, TreeLineTracker, full XSDUtils/CMXSDDocument) were only spot-checked via targeted searches rather than fully read.

Xerces feature defaults and whether XMLSchemaLoader honors external-general/parameter-entities for schema documents were not verified by executing the library; feature-name support is assumed from the project's own use of the same constants.

rejected_leads.lead: CacheResourcesManager.getResource / FilesUtils.isIncludedInDeployedPath: the containment check (normalize().startsWith(DEPLOYED_BASE_PATH)) is performed only after the early 'if (Files.exists(resourceCachePath)) return resourceCachePath;' branch, so a URI path containing '..' that resolves to an already-existing file outside ~/.lemminx (e.g. xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation="http://host/../../../../...") is returned as a readable grammar path.
rejected_leads.reason: The result is a path handed to the XML parser, not file content returned to the caller; practical impact is limited (parse behavior/presence only) and the ordering appears to be longstanding upstream code rather than a clear injected defect. Kept as unconfirmed lead, superseded by the XSD external-entity candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: CMXSDContentModelProvider.createCMDocument uses XSLoaderImpl.loadURI(key) (key derived from xsi:schemaLocation / xsi:noNamespaceSchemaLocation) with only an entity resolver set and no external-entity feature disabled, so content-model loading of an attacker-referenced schema may also resolve external entities (completion/hover path).
rejected_leads.reason: Same general root-cause class as the submitted candidate but a different sink; I did not verify XSLoaderImpl's default feature values from source, and the benchmark asks for one candidate, so it is reported only as a related unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: XMLValidator.isValidLocation opens new URL(resolvedLocation).openStream() on a schema location taken from the opened document (SSRF/local file probe), and XMLCacheResolverExtension/CacheResourcesManager download arbitrary http(s)/ftp resources by default.
rejected_leads.reason: Reachable only under the non-default schema validation mode 'onValidSchema', and downloading external resources is the documented feature with a download-external-resources setting; no content is returned by isValidLocation. Not chosen.

rejected_leads.lead: XMLServerSocketLauncher binds an unauthenticated LSP server on 0.0.0.0:5008.
rejected_leads.reason: Debug/socket launch mode only, not used by the default stdio launcher; appears to be intentional upstream behavior and requires the operator to choose that launcher. Not chosen.

rejected_leads.lead: XMLModelDeclaration.parse loops with 'for (int i = offset; i < length; i++)' instead of offset+length, truncating PI attribute parsing when the XMLString has a non-zero offset; MarkdownConverter uses reflection to add the 'file' protocol to jsoup allows; Constants.DOCUMENTATION_CONTENT regex with nested .* groups may be slow.
rejected_leads.reason: Functional/correctness or client-side rendering/hardening issues without a demonstrated attacker-controlled security impact in this snapshot; not chosen.

summary: Reviewed the Eclipse LemMinX (0.18.5-SNAPSHOT) main source tree (444 Java/resource files; only src/main is present in this snapshot, tests are absent). The strongest source-supported issue is XML External Entity (XXE) exposure in the XSD validation path: when a document is recognized as an XML Schema (by URI suffix or XML-Schema root namespace), XSDValidator builds a Xerces XMLGrammarPreparser and explicitly enables both external-general-entities and external-parameter-entities, ignoring the user's XMLValidationSettings (resolveExternalEntities defaults to false; disallowDocTypeDecl is likewise not consulted). This is reachable directly from textDocument/didOpen (validation is enabled by default), so opening a crafted XSD lets an attacker-controlled document trigger DTD/entity resolution: local file reads and server-side HTTP/FTP fetches via the resolver chain, with expanded values able to appear in Xerces-derived diagnostics/hover text, plus unbounded entity expansion in this parser (no Xerces SecurityManager / entityExpansionLimit is installed for this preparser, unlike LSPXMLParserConfiguration). One candidate is submitted; other leads are listed as rejected/unconfirmed.
